pr_title: expression: Fixing Expression Rewrite Bug in Predicate Push Down for NULLIF with Type Mismatch
pr_body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #57647

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?
The sql could be simplified as:
```sql
select *
from `t0`
where (
  nullif(3^1, case when (`c0`) then 91 end)
) in (select 1 from `t0`);
```

When rewriting the expression `nullif(3^1, case when (c0) then 91 end)`, it is transformed into:
`if(equals(3^1, case when (c0) then 91 end), null, 3^1)`.

When building this function, the` RetType` of `null` is inferred based on the type of `3^1`, and a new `RetType` is set.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/a82a3b41e7dee9b110dbac2ec18e7222f85ddefb/pkg/expression/builtin_control.go#L713-L720
Then, the SQL:

`where (nullif(3^1, case when (c0) then 91 end)) in (select 1 from t0);`
is rewritten to an inner join with otherConditions as:

`nullif(3^1, case when (c0) then 91 end) = 1.`

During `predicate push down`, it will try moving `otherConditions` into `equal conditions`: 
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/b11cce72848142c279842061285ed457846340c0/pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_join.go#L1564-L1572

But when rewriting the `equal condition`, the `RetType of null` has already been reset based on the earlier inference. So `re-inferring` of the `RetType` of null and 3^1 will not match previous result, and the type finally becomes `decimal`.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/a82a3b41e7dee9b110dbac2ec18e7222f85ddefb/pkg/expression/builtin_control.go#L279-L289

The constant 1 will be wrapped with a `(cast as decimal)`, making it no longer a column, which ultimately leads to the error.

I modified the `ifInferType4ControlFuncs()` method to determine whether a value is null. If a constant's `value.`k is null, it will also be treated as null.

@dash12653 I have some step-by-step debug on this issue, and I think the `null` constant value constructed when rewrite `nullif` to `if` has the right type(typeNull), and inside the first `InferType4ControlFuncs`, the `ret` type is inferred as `unsigned int`, so in `newBaseBuiltinFuncWithFieldTypes`, the first argument(the constant `null`) is expected to be converted to `unsigned longlong` type, however, `WrapWithCastAsInt` does not respect the unsigned flag, the `null` constant is converted to `longlong` type instead. In the second `InferType4ControlFuncs`, since the common type of `longlong` and `unsigned longlong`  is `decimal`, the `ret` type is inferred as `decimal`.
I think the root cause of this issue is that `WrapWithCastAsInt` does not respect unsigned flag, we should fix this issue by let `WrapWithCastAsInt` be aware of the unsigned flag of the target type.

Thank you for your detailed analysis, I really appreciate your time and guidance! Based on your analysis, I’m considering whether it might be better to modify `WrapWithCastAsInt` to accept `argTps[i]` as an additional parameter, so it can handle the `unsigned flag` directly. Do you think this would be a reasonable solution? Also, I did a check for `null values` at the end of each iteration, as shown below: Do you think this approach would be appropriate? Thanks again for your help.

Never mind, I realize I misunderstood the situation. The null value check was unnecessary and was a mistake. I could try modify `WrapWithCastAsInt` to handle the unsigned flag.

Hi @windtalker, after looking into it, I found that many places are doing a unified cast for different argument types(as shown below), and modifying `WrapWithCastAsInt` would require changing the signatures of other methods like `WrapWithCastAsReal`, `WrapWithCastAsString`, etc., even though they don’t actually use the additional parameter. https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/6180fb7358d216af3407a262cabb1b5ce322bd9f/pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go#L439-L466 I was thinking, instead of modifying the existing functions, could we write another `wrapCastAsInt` function who takes the target type as a parameter, and then call it in `newBaseBuiltinFuncWithTp`? This would allow us to handle the target type without introducing unnecessary changes. Thanks again for your time!

This would allow us to handle the target type without introducing unnecessary changes. > > Thanks again for your time! Looks like this is one of the technical debt in TiDB :( I think all the caller of `WrapWithCastAsInt` should provide extra information of whether the target type should be signed or unsigned. In fact, `WrapWithCastAsTime` has the same problem so `WrapWithCastAsTime` has the third parameter to indicate the target type is `Datetime` or `Timestamp`. I suggest to add an extra `tp *types.FieldTyp` parameter to `WrapWithCastAsInt`, if the caller does not have this information, then just pass nil, and inside `WrapWithCastAsInt`, we can handle the unsigned flag if input `tp` is not nil, and if the input `tp` is nil, then just keep current code logic. issue_context.title: Scalar function causes database crash.
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

1. schema.

```sql
create table `t0`
(
    `vkey` integer,
    `pkey` integer,
    `c0`   integer
);

insert into `t0`
values (1, 2, 3);
```



2. sql statement.

```sql
select *
from `t0`
where (nullif(
    3 ^ 10 & (abs(-50)) ,
    round(case when (((`t0`.`c0`) >= 1) or null) then 91 else 86 end)
    )) in (select `vkey` from `t0` where false);
```





### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

MySQL and TIDB have different execution results in the above case.

The normal result in MySQL 8:

```SQL
mysql> select *
    -> from `t0`
    -> where (nullif(
    ->     3 ^ 10 & (abs(-50)) ,
    ->     round(case when (((`t0`.`c0`) >= 1) or null) then 91 else 86 end)
    ->     )) in (select `vkey` from `t0` where false);
Empty set (0.00 sec)
```



TiDB should also return empty result, but failed.



### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

In TiDB v8.1.1:

```sql
MySQL [test]> select *
    -> from `t0`
    -> where (nullif(
    ->     3 ^ 10 & (abs(-50)) ,
    ->     round(case when (((`t0`.`c0`) >= 1) or null) then 91 else 86 end)
    ->     )) in (select `vkey` from `t0` where false);
ERROR 1105 (HY000): interface conversion: expression.Expression is *expression.ScalarFunction, not *expression.Column
```



TiDB crash when execute the same SQL statement.



### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

tidb v8.1.1
